title: Pay via AmEx at Any Merchant That Accepts Visa via EatClub Caviar Reserve (Subscription Costs $11.99/Mo or $119/Yr) @ EatClub
body:

It's lovely to hear you're interested in joining Caviar Reserve! 💛
At the moment, Caviar Reserve isn't available to everyone just yet. Access is currently limited to eligible customers who previously joined the waitlist.
You can learn more about the membership and its benefits here:
https://eatclub.com.au/caviar-reserve
We appreciate your interest and hope to welcome more members in the near future!
[jaysonphillips] Probably good if you were going to buy the subscription anyway, but if you mostly cook at home, you essentially have to spend $1000 a month every month of the year to make this worth it…

But not earning points?
Did I get this right?
[reivaxX] @royale: You need to be on the saffron or caviar (free) rewards tier to be able to use eatclub to pay at aldi, and you also earn 1% and 2% dining credit respectively
[whyisave] @reivaxX:
the saffron or caviar (free) rewards tier to be able to use eatclub to pay at aldi
That's some Inception-level ways to get a some bucks back, into Eatclub…which still needs a way to claim that dining credit :)
[AllyOop] @royale: 3% cashback at Aldi, Woolies and Coles
[reivaxX] This is a good deal to make back the subscription fee and earn Amex points. However I have recently come across them declining all payments when you reach the $1000 cap that month or that payment will put you over the $1000.
Their T's and C's intend for you to just stop earning dining credit after you earn $10 each month, however the system currently declines all payments. So it is almost impossible to fully break even considering they don't have a tracker in app to show how much you've spent that month
[Oh Boy] That's a bummer! As long as they let you spend over 1k each month I am okay with no cashback
[T-man] me too, especially since I spend so much at Costco, $1k is quite a low monthly spending limit.
[whyisave] I spend so much at Costco, $1k is quite a low monthly spending limit.
That's a flex.
[playbargain] Card limits apply; up to $1,000 a month on everyday spend and separately, up to $1,000 a month on grocery spend.
Spend that earns at the Earn Anytime rate, the 2% restaurant rate, the grocery rate or under partner earn does not count towards this cap.
So,
- $1000 limit on groceries
- No limit on Restaurant spend.
- No limit on Partner spend.
- $1000 limit everything (almost) else.

[UnrealMacaw] https://eatclub.com.au/terms
Warning, eatclub charge 1 to 6% service fee on every transaction, think this should be added to the description

[UnrealMacaw] Service” means the EatClub app, website, EatClub Card, EatClub Premium, and all related services provided by EatClub;
EatClub charges a Service Fee on Transactions made using the Service. The Service Fee is calculated as a percentage of the Transaction amount, ranging between one percent (1%) and six percent (6%), with a minimum fee of twenty cents ($0.20 AUD).

[Financefiend] Maximum ‘Earn Anywhere’ dining credit rewards is $10 a month (1% for $1000 max spend). Excluded merchant categories for Earn Anywhere https://eatclub.com.au/caviar-reserve/merchant-categories
• Government services: ATO, AusPost, PostBillPay, many council rates, Urban Utilities, fines, AHPRA, court fees, child support
• Utilities (gas, electricity, water)
• Insurance
• Cash, quasi-cash, stored value, pre-paid load, financial institutions, crypto, security brokers, money transfers
• Gambling
• Jewellery, pawn shops, stamp & coin shops
• Mobile and telecoms
• Real estate agents - rentals
• Drs, dentists, optometrists, hospitals miscell 8099, chiro, podiatrists, labs
• Education, schools
• Car dealers, automotive service shops, auto repair shops, parking garages and meters
• Public transport (bus, rail, ferry)
• Charities, political organisations
• Timeshares, dating services/escorts
• Theatrical producers and ticket agencies
• Food delivery aggregators (eg. Uber Eats, Doordash, Menulog)
• Banks, credit & debit card providers (e.g. Zip, Revolut. Afterpay per above poster)
• Transactions over $500
“Fuel and travel” is eligible spend.
